slides.title: Core values guide everyday behavior.
slides.headline: Core values guide everyday behavior.
notes: Values are the team’s handful of behavioral rules. They remain useful when decisions are difficult.
Review established values today. If none exist, do not create them today.
Shannon describes values as alive, constant behavioral rules with consequences for violations.
Review where values shape real decisions. Address repeated violations through the company’s established people process.
This workshop reviews existing values; it does not create a new dismissal process.
slides.support: Core values remain consistent as the business grows.
body: Use them in decisions. Hold one another accountable for the behavior.

slides.title: What are your organization’s core values?
slides.headline: What are your organization’s core values?
notes: Circle’s Kick Off checklist calls for reviewing values when they already exist. Ask for concrete behaviors. If the company has no established values, do not create them here.
slides.support: Not aspirational. How your best people already act.
body: Is it a value you hire and fire on, or a brand value?
When did you last let someone go for not living it?
Does someone who keeps breaching it belong here?
Would you build a new company around it, in any industry?
